blocks.fullContent: Session opens on the Forge Sheet build kickoff. All three provings completed this heat: FLY-72 (inline storage decided), FLY-73 (Stop hook confirmed), FLY-74 (semantic audit v1 scope confirmed). FLY-75 (state format schema) is the active task.

blocks.digest: Inline storage: fullContent is required in every block — not optional.
digestPoints: fullContent is stored inline and required in every block
one session is about 24 KB; thirty sessions parse in about 7 ms
reference storage rejected — complexity with no benefit at this scale
blocks.fullContent: Decision from FLY-72: store fullContent inline in state.json as a required field. At 30 blocks per session, one session is 24.4 KB. At 30 sessions, 732 KB — JSON.parse completes in ~7ms. Reference storage rejected: adds complexity with no benefit at this scale. P2 (passage detail) reads fullContent directly from state.json without a secondary fetch.

blocks.digest: Stop hook fires once per exchange. Sidecar heartbeat pattern confirmed for the heuristic alarm.
blocks.fullContent: Decision from FLY-73: the Stop Claude Code hook event fires exactly once per conversational exchange — after all tool calls within the turn complete. Empirically confirmed: one exchange with ~10 tool calls produced one Stop hook invocation. Alarm design: Stop hook compares state.json mtime against a sidecar heartbeat file. If state.json not updated this exchange, write an alert sidecar. Shell polls both; alarm banner renders when alert count ≥ 2.

blocks.digest: Semantic audit is v1 scope. Session JSONL readable mid-session; Haiku at $0.003/audit.
blocks.fullContent: Decision from FLY-74: semantic audit is v1 scope, not post-v1. The session JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/[dir]/[session-id].jsonl is readable mid-session without locking. An independent claude haiku -p call correctly identifies omissions from a mock conversation. Cost: ~$0.003/audit (~$1/year). Cadence: on demand + at session end (Banking the Fire). projectSlug must be a top-level field in state.json so the audit script can find the correct state file.

blocks.digest: Does the state.json schema need a createdAt timestamp at the session level for the P3 collapse label?
blocks.fullContent: Open question surfaced during schema design: P3 (sheet at rest) shows prior sessions collapsed with a date label. The schema has a 'date' field on each session (string, e.g. '2026-08-01'). Is that sufficient for the collapsed label, or does the shell need a more precise timestamp (e.g. to show '14 days ago')? The date string is sufficient for the initial build — relative time formatting can be added later without a schema change.

blocks.digest: State schema is locked. FLY-76 (shell P1) can begin immediately after this task ships.
blocks.fullContent: The state.json schema is now canonical and locked for v1. The four fixture files cover all four captured states. FLY-76 (shell P1 — live sheet) is unblocked and can begin. The Engineer's first action in FLY-76: build the shell against the live.json fixture and verify all block kinds render with correct visual treatment.

blocks.digest: The resurfacing promise ships untested. Risk accepted — instrument it so a miss is visible, not silent.
blocks.fullContent: The sheet promises to resurface settled decisions when a conversation touches them, and that ability is unproven. Put to the human as a High risk: if wrong, the builder delegates on the strength of a net that catches only sometimes. The human accepted the risk and chose to proceed without a proving. Condition of acceptance: resurfacing is instrumented from day one — every decision-record check is logged, so a miss is countable rather than silent.

risk.stake: if wrong — the builder trusts a net that catches only sometimes

blocks.digest: The two-week trial could end without a single unprompted return. Accept that risk before the shell build continues?
blocks.fullContent: Put to you before the shell build continues: the two-week usage trial may end without a single unprompted return to the sheet. If that happens, the shell work done in the meantime was built on an unvalidated habit. Accept the risk and continue, or hold the build until the first week reports.

risk.stake: if wrong — a fortnight of shell work leans on a habit that never formed

blocks.digest: Correction: the audit cadence is on demand plus heat handover — not hourly, as earlier stated.
blocks.fullContent: Correction to the earlier semantic audit note: the cadence decided in FLY-74 is on demand plus at heat handover. The 'hourly' figure mentioned in passing was wrong and is superseded.

blocks.digest: The session JSONL keeps growing mid-write but never locks — safe to read at any moment.
blocks.fullContent: Empirical observation from the audit proving: the session JSONL at ~/.claude/projects/ grows while Claude writes but is never locked. Reading mid-session returned valid lines every time across twenty attempts.

blocks.digest: If the sheet ever renders for two people at once, whose glance does the hero serve?
blocks.fullContent: Speculative: the sheet is designed for one builder, but Forge is open source. If two people ever watch the same session, the hero's 'what needs you' framing has two answers. Not a v1 question — noted so it isn't lost.

# Context: Forge Sheet
Domain glossary — pure definitions, no implementation details.

## The sheet

The rendered page the builder reads on his second monitor. One continuous accreting document per project; all sessions grouped on it. "The sheet" refers to both the HTML shell when rendered and the metaphor it is built on (the physical drafting sheet a designer works on).
_Avoid:_ "the viewer", "the companion app", "the dashboard".

## state.json

One JSON file per project that Forge Sheet reads from. It is the sole source of truth the shell renders. Claude writes it during sessions; the shell polls it. It accretes across sessions.
_Avoid:_ "the database", "the data file", "session file".

## Content kind

The classification of a passage's role in the session. Seven named kinds plus a mandatory fallback. Determines how a passage renders on the sheet (its attention tier and visual treatment).
_Avoid:_ "content type", "message category".

## Untyped

The mandatory fallback content kind. Anything unclassifiable renders as untyped.

## Quench / quenched

Resolution of an agent or concern. Agents are "quenched" when their work on the project is done; concerns are "quenched" when resolved. Quenched marks cool into the warm-grey ramp visually — they remain in the margin but visually recede.
_Avoid:_ "done", "resolved", "completed", "closed" when referring to Forge Sheet states.

## At heat

An agent currently writing in the active session. Heat increases with time at work — an agent that has been writing for 25 minutes is hotter than one that just started. The roster communicates this through the incandescence heat system.
_Avoid:_ "active", "running", "in progress" when referring to the roster state.

## Smoke alarm

The two-tier coverage system that detects when the sheet may be falling behind the session. Tier 1: heuristic (hook-based, always on — fires when exchanges pass without state updates). Tier 2: semantic audit (independent Claude call — compares conversation against sheet). When either tier fires, a banner appears on the sheet.

## Semantic audit

The second tier of the smoke alarm. An independent Claude call that reads both the conversation record and the current sheet and identifies omissions. It is independent of the sheet-writing skill — a key constraint: an audit that shares the writer's blind spots cannot catch them.

## Passage detail

The drill-down view (P2). Full-density content behind a single passage, opened by clicking the passage or its digest line. One action returns the reader to their exact previous position. The escape hatch that makes trusting the digest safe.
_Avoid:_ "drill-down view", "detail pane", "expanded view".

## Heat system

The colour system for Forge Sheet's accent. Grounded in black-body incandescence — a smith reads metal readiness by colour. Ember (#C22400) → cherry (#E62E0F) → furnace (#FF7A1A) → lemon (#FFC940). Heat = now and energy. Quench = resolve, marks cool to the warm-grey ramp.
_Avoid:_ "colour system", "accent system", "theme".
